problems.title: The interpolation metric is L1 rather than the described L2
problems.source_location: Eqs.(6)–(7), PDF p.8; approximation Appendix/Table A.4; _compute_anchor_weight_entry
claim: Placeholder distances use mean absolute tensor differences, while the method and norm ablation identify Euclidean weighting.
analysis: Use two identical layers, one token, query \((0,0)\), anchors A=\((0,20)\), B=\((11,11)\), temperature \(1\). Full Euclidean distances are \(\sqrt{800}\approx28.2843\) and \(22\), giving weights approximately \((0.001862,0.998138)\), entropy \(0.01957\) bits below the default \(0.3\) threshold. Reuse is admitted. Placeholder mean absolute distances are instead \(10,11\), giving \((0.731059,0.268941)\) and reversing anchor preference. For offset values \(0,10\), the interpolated coordinate changes from about \(9.98138\) to \(2.68941\). Positive-temperature rescaling cannot repair a reversed ordering.
result: The accepted-input release is a hybrid metric, not the stated L2 interpolation. Actual cache prevalence, performance and table-producing commit are unresolved.
repair: Either use an explicitly defined Euclidean reduction or describe the hybrid admission/prefix/placeholder metrics and match the ablation configuration.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local implementation or interpretation defect; damage to the central empirical result has not been established.

problems.title: Activation cutoff differs from conventional top-p selection
problems.source_location: Section 3.3 and cache-maintenance Algorithm 1; predict_as_anchor, lines 1041–1055
claim: The source uses the last cumulative sum below \(p\), and selects all anchors when no cumulative sum is below \(p\).
analysis: At \(p=0.9\), weights \((0.95,0.05)\) select both anchors, while \((0.60,0.35,0.05)\) select only the first with mass \(0.60\). Conventional nucleus selection would select one and two respectively. The first case can pass the entropy admission gate. These counts affect future eviction, not current interpolation weights. The paper does not define activation as conventional nucleus selection.
result: The threshold discontinuity is established, but classification as an unintended defect requires the missing activation contract.
repair: If standard nucleus selection is intended, retain the smallest prefix reaching mass \(p\), including its crossing element. This conditional correction is not an accuracy guarantee.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.
problems.impact_rationale: Unspecified maintenance semantics prevent a supported paper-error rating.

problems.title: Low relative entropy does not bound absolute distance
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, entropy admission Eq.(5); conditional Lipschitz propositions
claim: Low entropy is used as a reuse-confidence heuristic; its mathematical information is relative anchor preference.
analysis: For anchors \(0,10\) and every scalar query \(q>10\), distances are \((q,q-10)\). Their softmax weights and entropy remain fixed, with entropy about \(0.00072045\) bits, while nearest distance grows without bound. For the \(1\)-Lipschitz offset \(F(q)=q\), interpolation remains near \(9.999546\); queries \(20,100,1000\) have errors about \[10.000454,90.000454,990.000454\]. This is a function-class witness, not an asserted unbounded ray in an actual finite-vocabulary model.
result: The heuristic does not supply an absolute-radius guarantee. The paper’s conditional distance bounds are not contradicted.
problems.existing_correction_status: No paper correction is required for this cleared concern.
problems.impact_rationale: A scope clarification; no explicit universal accuracy theorem is refuted.

problems.title: First-token latency is already included in the current table
problems.source_location: Section 4.3 correction footnote and Table 2, PDF p.9
claim: The authors disclose an earlier omission and report updated latency components.
analysis: Agent \(5\) has \(17.5+21.1+16.2=54.8\) ms, and \(428.6/54.8\approx7.82117\), matching \(7.82\). The five rounded speedups agree with component sums. These are TTFT/prefill results; ordinary decoding is not accelerated and full-response speedup is not inferred.
result: No current-table arithmetic error is established; the earlier omission was already corrected by the authors.
problems.existing_correction_status: The authors explicitly disclosed and incorporated the first-token correction in the inspected versions.
problems.impact_rationale: Cleared current evidence; a historical fixed issue does not inflate severity.

problems.title: Universal quality preservation exceeds the reported results
problems.source_location: Abstract and Section 3.1; Table 1, PDF p.8; Table A.2 and AIME discussion
claim: The paper describes operation without quality degradation across its workload results.
analysis: HumanEval with two Qwen-Coder agents changes \(86.3\%\to81.4\%\), a decrease of \(4.9\) percentage points. Other reported configurations decline, including AIME by \(9.2\) points, while some improve or tie. The appendix acknowledges a resource/decoding-length explanation for AIME; it does not erase the observed loss. Rounded point estimates alone do not establish statistical significance or isolate the cache approximation’s causal effect.
result: The supported evidence is heterogeneous performance, not universal preservation. No benchmark result is remeasured or declared fabricated.
repair: Qualify preservation by configuration and acknowledge reported accuracy/resource tradeoffs. Matched output-budget evidence is needed for a causal explanation.
